About this manual#

HDX Inspect is an app for inspecting machinery and equipment in the field, capturing sign-off from the inspector and the customer, and producing a branded PDF certificate for each machine. It runs on Windows, Android and iOS, and it works with or without an internet connection.

This manual is task-oriented. It walks through everything an inspector or office administrator does day to day — from signing in, through a complete inspection, to distributing and correcting certificates, managing the schedule, writing quotes and invoices, and configuring the app. It describes HDX Inspect v4.3.0.

Who should read it#

  • Inspectors — perform checks in the field, capture photos and readings, and obtain signatures. See Getting started, Performing an inspection, and Reports.
  • Administrators / office staff — additionally manage customers, machines, templates, accounts, the shared Google Drive folder, scheduling and billing. Admin-only features are marked (Admin) throughout.

How to read the call-out boxes#

Three kinds of highlighted box appear in this manual:

Tip

A practical suggestion that makes a task easier or avoids a common mistake.

Important — read this

A point you must not miss — usually about losing access, losing work, or an action that cannot be undone.

Good to know

Something the app deliberately leaves to you — a decision, a check or a responsibility that stays with your organisation.

What's new in v4.3.0#

  • Delivery notes are created automatically. The work hours, travel time and distance you record on an inspection become lines on the visit's delivery note as soon as the inspection is finalised (chapter 11).
  • Easier navigation on phones. The bottom bar holds every destination and scrolls sideways, and you can swipe across the screen to move between destinations (§2.7).
  • An introduction, hints and this manual in the app. A short introduction on first sign-in, a one-time hint on each main screen and a ? button that opens this manual at the right chapter (§2.9).
  • Company profile branding. Large logos are scaled down automatically, the logo has three print sizes, a letterhead banner image can be added, and the slogan, footer lines and banner can be aligned (§13.3).
  • Checklist templates can be archived and restored (§10.3).
  • Sync recovers by itself after a dropped connection, and Settings has a Re-check Drive store action (§13.6, chapter 14).

Keep all devices on the same version

When a new version of the app is released, update every device your organisation uses before carrying on with normal work. A device that is still on an older version may stop syncing and ask to be updated. Nothing is lost — work on that device continues and syncs again once it is updated.

1. Introduction#

1.1 What HDX Inspect does#

An inspector selects a customer and one of their machines, completes the machine's checklist (marking each item Pass, Fail or N/A), records the machine's hours or mileage and the work and travel for the visit, and captures signatures from both the inspector and the customer. The completed check is stored as a dated record and a numbered PDF certificate is generated in the customer's language (German or English). The office or the inspector then shares or prints that certificate — the app itself sends no e-mail.

It replaces a paper-based process. The office can also plan visits in a calendar, see which machines are due, and write quotes, delivery notes and invoices.

1.2 The two roles#

HDX Inspect has two roles. The customer is not a user of the app — they only sign on the inspector's device at completion and are given the PDF by your organisation.

RoleWhat they can do
Admin /
Office		Everything an inspector can do, plus: manage customers, machines and machine types; create and edit checklist templates; manage user accounts and devices; set up the shared Google Drive folder; manage company profiles and certificate settings; schedule bookings; void and reissue certificates; write quotes and invoices; and use the data-retention and device-wipe tools.
InspectorView bookings; perform checks in the field; capture photos, machine readings, work and travel; sign and obtain the customer's sign-off; view and distribute certificates; create and sign delivery notes — plus any admin abilities an administrator has individually granted to them (§13.9).

Good to know

Roles and permissions control what each person can do in the app. Who can open the shared Google Drive folder is a separate matter, managed in Google Drive by your administrator. Anyone who can open that folder can reach the data in it, whatever their role in the app — so share it only with the people and accounts your organisation trusts with all of it.

1.3 Where your data is kept#

  • On each device. Your records, photos, signatures and certificates are stored on the device in protected form. Everything you capture is saved on the device before the app confirms it, so you can keep working without a connection.
  • In your organisation's Google Drive. An administrator chooses one shared Google Drive folder. Every device sends its changes there and receives everyone else's — this is what keeps your devices in step. Certificates are also filed there as PDFs, by year, with the customer and machine in the file name so they are easy to find.
  • Signing in and Google are separate. You sign in to the app with an app account (username and password). Google is connected separately, by an administrator, only to give the app access to the shared folder.

The publisher of the app has no access to your data. The Privacy policy linked in the app explains this in full.

1.4 The demo#

A device that has not been set up yet can be used with sample data instead of your organisation's data (§2.1). In the demo nothing is synced: the Google connection, the shared folder and recording certificate handoffs are switched off. It is meant for training and for trying the app. Settings → Sync & Drive shows whether a device is in demo mode.

2. Getting started#

2.1 Trying the app without an account — “Try the demo”#

On a device that has not been set up yet, the Set up this device screen offers Try the demo. Tap it to load sample customers, machines, bookings and checklists onto this device and sign in as a demo administrator. Everything works as in the real app — you can run a complete inspection through to a PDF certificate — but nothing leaves the device: the sync badge reads Demo data · not synced and the Google and Drive settings are hidden.

To leave the demo, open Settings → Danger zone → Exit demo and erase sample data. This erases the sample data and everything captured during the demo. A final screen then offers Close app; the next launch shows the setup screen again. The demo is only offered while the device has no real account.

In the demo, do not use Sign out — there is no demo password to sign back in with. If you did, close and reopen the app; it signs the demo administrator in again.

Tip

The Privacy policy and the User manual are linked at the bottom of the setup screen and under Settings → Help & about. They open in your browser.

2.2 First run — create the first administrator#

The very first time HDX Inspect runs on a new device there are no accounts yet, so instead of the sign-in screen it shows Set up this device with Set up a new organisation and Join an existing store (§2.3). For the very first device in your organisation, choose Set up a new organisation; this creates the first administrator account.

  1. Choose Set up a new organisation.
  2. Enter the administrator's Full name and a Username.
  3. Optionally enter an Email address.
  4. Choose a Password of at least 12 characters and type it again to confirm. It must use at least five different characters and must not contain an obvious word such as “password” or “123456”. Use the eye icon to reveal what you typed.
  5. Tap Create administrator. The account is created and you are taken straight into the app.

Tip

Use a long password that you use nowhere else, and give every person their own account. Create each account once, from a device that is already set up (Settings → Accounts & devices, §13.8); the same account is then used on every device that person works on.

2.3 Adding another device#

All of your organisation's devices share one Google Drive folder. To bring a new device into use you do not create new accounts on it — you connect it to the same folder and let the existing accounts, customers, machines and history arrive by sync. People then sign in with the account they already have.

On the new device, choose Join an existing store on the Set up this device screen, then work through the steps it shows:

  1. Connect Google — sign in with the same Google account your other devices use. (This gives the app access to the shared folder only; it is not your app login.)
  2. Choose the shared store — tap Find the existing store to locate your organisation's “HDX Inspect Data Store” folder automatically, or Enter folder ID to paste the folder ID the office already uses.
  3. Sync and sign in — tap Sync and continue. The device fetches your organisation's data, including the user accounts, and then shows the normal sign-in screen.
  4. Sign in with your own account — the one an administrator created for you (§13.8). From then on it also works without a connection.

Don't recreate accounts per device

Do not try to get “the same account on two devices” by creating an account with the same name on the new device. That is a second, separate account which merely shares the name and does not see the original's history. Join the store as described above and sign in with the existing account.

Tip

One account can sign in on as many devices as a person needs. Joining a store needs an internet connection the first time, so the data can be fetched.

“No accounts yet” on a team that already uses the app

If the app says the store has no accounts yet although your organisation already uses the app, you are probably connected with a different Google account, and a new, empty folder was created. Go back, connect the right Google account and try again — do not set up a first administrator. (If this really is your organisation's first device, the app offers to set up the first administrator instead.)

The Google account needs edit access to the shared folder. With view-only access the app stops and asks you to have the folder shared with edit access, then to join again.

2.4 Signing in#

  1. Enter your Username and Password.
  2. Tap Sign in. If the details are wrong, an error appears in red. After five wrong passwords in a row the account is locked on that device for 15 minutes.

You can sign in without an internet connection, so field work continues offline.

If you cannot sign in, tap Trouble signing in? below the Sign in button. It explains how password resets work (an administrator resets your password to a temporary one — see §2.6 and §13.8) and, when the device is connected, offers Check for account updates, which fetches the latest account data so that a password reset made on another device reaches this one before you sign in.

2.5 Face ID / fingerprint or PIN sign-in#

So you do not have to type your full password every time, HDX Inspect can remember your login on a device in one of two ways: the device's biometrics (Face ID, Touch ID or a fingerprint) and/or a short device PIN. Both are optional, both apply to one device only, and neither replaces your password.

Biometrics. On a device that has Face ID / Touch ID / a fingerprint set up, an Enable Face ID sign-in on this device option is ticked by default below the password box. Leave it ticked and sign in as normal. Next time, tap Sign in as <your username> with Face ID (or fingerprint) and confirm with your face or finger.

PIN. Useful on any device, including desktops. On the sign-in screen tap Set PIN, choose a 4–12 digit PIN and confirm it, then sign in as usual to save it. Next time, tap Sign in with PIN. Simple PINs (all the same digit, a run such as 1234 and a few well-known patterns) are refused, and a PIN must not already be used by another account on the device. Five wrong PINs lock PIN sign-in on that device for 15 minutes (your password still works). You can set up either method under Settings → Security; switching one on asks for your password once.

Shared devices. Each person can set up their own PIN on the same device — the app recognises whose PIN was typed. Biometric sign-in is different: a device remembers only one account's Face ID / fingerprint at a time, so the button names the account it will sign in to, and turning it on for a second account asks you to confirm before it replaces the first.

Things to know about quick sign-in

Sensitive actions still ask for your password: voiding or superseding a certificate, the account and device tools, the retention purge, the device wipe and deleting your account. A PIN is never accepted for those.

If you change your password, biometric sign-in keeps working and any PIN is cleared — set a new one. If your password was reset on another device, quick sign-in stops working here: sign in once with the new password and set it up again.

2.6 Changing your password#

First login with a temporary password. When an administrator creates your account they give you a temporary password. The first time you sign in with it, the app asks you to set your own:

  1. Re-enter the temporary password once more.
  2. Choose a new password (at least 12 characters) and confirm it.
  3. Tap Save password. You are then taken into the app.

Changing it later. Open Settings → Account → Change my password. Enter your current password, then your new password twice. The new password must be at least 12 characters and differ from the current one.

Deleting your own account. Open Settings → Danger zone → Delete my account. The app explains what happens, then asks for your password. Deletion removes your login from every device in the organisation and signs you out. The inspection records and certificates you created stay with the organisation. It cannot be undone. If you are the organisation's last active administrator, the app refuses: create a second administrator account first (§13.8).

2.7 Finding your way around#

After signing in you land on the main screen. Navigation is on the left as a rail on wide screens (tablets in landscape, desktop) and along the bottom as a bar on narrow screens (phones).

On a phone the bottom bar holds every destination. They do not all fit on the screen at once, so the bar scrolls sideways: slide the bar itself to the left to bring the later destinations into view, then tap the one you want. The half-visible icon at the edge of the bar is the hint that there is more to scroll to. The highlighted destination is always kept in view.

The bar respects your phone's font size setting: with a larger font each destination is made wide enough for its name to stay on one line, so fewer destinations are visible at once.

You can also swipe left or right across the screen to move to the next or previous destination. On a Windows PC with a narrow window, scroll the bar by dragging it with the mouse or by turning the mouse wheel over it.

The top of every main screen shows the screen title, a ? button that opens this manual at the matching chapter, a sync badge (Online, N queued, Syncing…, Offline, Sync issue or N need attention) — tap it to open Settings, or Sync conflicts when some are waiting — and a circle with your initials.

The destinations are:

DestinationWhat it is forWho sees it
DashboardYour daily overview and quick actions.Everyone
BookingsThe calendar of scheduled visits.Everyone
MachinesThe machine register.Everyone
ReportsCompleted certificates.Everyone
CustomersThe customer register.Everyone
RemindersMachines that are due or overdue.Everyone
BillingQuotes, delivery notes and invoices (chapters 11–12). Called Belege in German.Everyone
TemplatesThe checklist template editor.Admin, or an inspector granted Templates
SettingsAccount, language, sync and admin tools.Everyone

2.8 Signing out#

Open Settings and tap Sign out at the bottom, then confirm. Signing out deletes nothing.

Sync only runs while someone is signed in. If the sync badge shows queued work, wait until it reads Online before signing out; otherwise that work stays on the device until the next sign-in.

2.9 Getting help: the introduction, hints and this manual#

  • The introduction. The first time you sign in on a device, a short introduction explains how to find your way around, how an inspection runs, how offline working and sync fit together, and where to find help. Swipe or tap Next to move through it, Skip to leave it, and Done on the last page.
  • Hints. After the introduction, each main screen shows a one-time hint under its title. Learn more opens the matching chapter of this manual; Got it hides the hint for good.
  • The ? button at the top of every main screen opens this manual at the chapter for the screen you are on.
  • The whole manual. Settings → Help & about → User manual opens it from the beginning. The same link is on the first-run screen, next to the privacy policy.
  • Seeing it again. Settings → Help & about → Show the introduction again replays the introduction and brings every hint back.

The introduction and the hints are remembered per person and per device, so a colleague who signs in on the same tablet gets their own. Once you have finished or skipped the introduction it does not come back by itself.

Good to know

The manual is a web page in English, opened in your browser, and needs an internet connection. A PDF copy can be downloaded from the top of the manual page for offline reading. The introduction and the hints themselves work offline.

3. The Dashboard#

The Dashboard greets you by name and gathers the things that need attention into one screen. Pull down to refresh it.

  • New check — starts an inspection (§4.1). Users who may manage bookings also see New booking.
  • Status cards — Overdue and Due ≤ 30 days (tap for Reminders), Bookings this week (tap for Bookings) and Draft checks. Overdue and Due ≤ 30 days leave out machines that already have an open booking.
  • Reinspection required — machines whose most recent certificate is a Blocking fail. A later passing check clears the machine from this list.
  • Today — today's visits with customer, start time and number of machines; tap one to open the booking.
  • Resume drafts — checks on this device that are not finalised yet. Tap a draft to carry on, or use the three-dot menu → Discard draft.
  • Recent results — the most recently finalised checks; tap one to open its certificate.
  • Open quotes and Unpaid invoices (users with the Billing permission) — tap either to open the Billing tab.
  • Attention cards appear only when something needs it — for example a certificate or document PDF that could not be created yet (with Retry now), a delivery note that could not be created (§11.2), a document number issued twice (§12.7), or a checklist template that lacks text in the working language.

Tip

Every change in a check is saved on the device as you make it, so you can always come back to a draft from here — even after a flat battery.

4. Performing an inspection#

This is the heart of the app. A check moves through a fixed sequence of screens: select machine → checklist → machine data → summary → signatures → completion. You can leave at any point and resume later from the Dashboard or the booking.

4.1 Starting a check#

There are four ways to start:

  • From a Booking — open the booking and tap Start next to a machine (or Resume if a draft already exists). This is the normal route for planned work, and the only one that links the check to the booking (§6.2).
  • From a Reminder — book the machine first, then start it from the booking.
  • From New check on the Dashboard — pick the customer, then the machine.
  • From a machine — open it in Machines and tap Start inspection.

A sheet first asks Which inspection? — Acceptance inspection or Recurring inspection (§4.2) — with the likely kind pre-selected and marked Suggested. Tap Continue. A machine can have only one unfinished draft: if it already has one, that draft resumes instead. When your organisation has more than one company profile, the same sheet also asks which company the check is issued under (§13.3).

The app then loads the machine's checklist — the template chosen on that machine if one is set (§9.2), otherwise the default template of its machine type. The check keeps its own copy of the items, so later changes to the template never alter this record. If the machine has no checklist, or its checklist is empty, the check does not start and the message says what has to be added under Templates (chapter 10).

4.2 Acceptance vs recurring inspection#

Every check records which kind of inspection it is, following the Austrian Arbeitsmittelverordnung (AM-VO):

  • Acceptance inspection (Abnahmeprüfung, § 7 AM-VO) — before a machine is first put into service, and after it has been set up at another location or substantially modified.
  • Recurring inspection (wiederkehrende Prüfung, § 8 AM-VO) — the regular periodic inspection, at least once per calendar year and at most 15 months apart.

The sheet pre-selects Acceptance for a machine with no recorded inspection yet and Recurring for one that has been inspected before; you can always choose the other. On the Summary screen the kind can still be changed until you sign. The certificate states the kind in bold beneath its title — for example RECURRING INSPECTION (§ 8 AM-VO) / WIEDERKEHRENDE PRÜFUNG (§ 8 AM-VO) — and a small chip shows it in lists throughout the app.

A passed acceptance inspection sets the machine's last-check and next-due dates exactly like a recurring inspection.

Good to know

The certificate states the inspection kind as recorded by the inspector. Whether the inspector holds the qualification the law requires for that kind of inspection remains your organisation's responsibility.

4.3 Completing the checklist#

Each item is a numbered card with its label and (where given) a description. A header bar shows the customer, machine type and your progress. If the machine had defects on its last check, a banner lists them at the top so you can confirm they have been put right. For every item:

  1. Tap Pass, Fail or N/A. Your choice is saved immediately; tapping the same answer again clears it.
  2. If you tap Fail, a dialog asks you to classify the defect as Blocking or Minor.
  3. Type any Notes in the field below. For a failed item a description of the defect is required.
  4. Add photos with the camera button. On a phone or tablet you can take a photo or choose from the gallery; on desktop you pick a file. Tap a thumbnail to mark it up (see below). To delete a photo, tap the small × on it or long-press it and confirm.

While anything is still missing, the header shows an orange N open issues chip and the Continue — machine data button stays disabled. Tap the chip or Next open item to jump to the first item that needs attention, or switch on Only open items to hide everything already complete. When every rule is met, tap Continue — machine data.

Marking up a photo

Tap a photo to open the annotation editor and point out a defect on the image itself. You can draw freehand, or add an arrow, rectangle, ellipse or a short text tag, in any of five colours. Undo removes the last mark, Clear removes them all; then tap Save. The original photo is kept unchanged, and the marked-up version appears on the certificate. Photos can be annotated only until the check is signed.

Checklist rules

The app will not let you finalise a check unless these rules are met — it never passes an item for you:

• Every item must be answered.

• A Fail needs a defect classification (Blocking or Minor), a note, and at least one photo.

• On a photo-required item, a Pass needs at least one photo — or, if a photo is genuinely impossible in the field, a note explaining why. An N/A needs an explanatory note.

Notes are saved automatically a moment after you stop typing. If a note cannot be saved, the app tells you and lets you retry before you move on.

Defect severity drives the result

Blocking means the machine fails and a reinspection is required — its next-due date is brought forward. Minor means “Pass with defects”: the defect is recorded and shown again at the next check, with the normal next-due date.

4.4 Recording machine data#

The Machine data & time screen captures meter readings and the visit's work and travel. Which reading fields appear depends on what the machine type tracks:

  • Operating hours — shown and required if the type tracks hours.
  • Odometer (km) — shown if the type tracks kilometres.
  • Work time, Travel time and Travel distance — these become the lines of the visit's delivery note when the inspection is finalised (chapter 11). Times are entered in decimal hours (1.5 = 1 h 30 min).

The reading fields start with the machine's last recorded values — overwrite them with today's reading. If a reading is lower than the last one recorded, the app asks for a reason (for example a replaced meter) before it accepts it with Use this reading. Tap Continue — summary when done.

4.5 Reviewing the summary#

The Summary screen shows the overall result as a coloured banner — green PASS, amber PASS — MINOR DEFECTS, or red FAIL — together with a count of passed / minor / blocking / N/A items, the customer and machine details, the date, the readings and the work and travel figures. Failed items are listed with their severity and notes. While something still needs attention, an orange banner names the reason instead and the Sign & complete button is disabled — tap the banner to go back to the first open item.

Certificate language

The summary carries a Certificate language control (Deutsch / English). The check starts in the customer's preferred language (§8.1), and you can switch it here until you sign. This sets the language of the whole PDF certificate; it is independent of the app's own interface language (§13.1). A certificate can be finalised only if the checklist has text in that language for every item — if not, switch the certificate language or have an administrator add the missing template text (chapter 10).

Important — read this

Once you sign, the certificate is locked and can no longer be edited in the app. After that, a mistake can only be put right by voiding or superseding the certificate (§5.4–5.5). Check the summary carefully before signing.

4.6 Signatures#

Tapping Sign & complete collects two signatures in turn on the device's signature pad. Draw with a finger or stylus; use Undo to remove the last stroke or Clear to start again, then tap Confirm.

  1. Inspector signature — you sign first.
  2. Customer sign-off — the customer enters their name and signs, confirming the declaration shown above the signature pad: that the inspection was performed and the results, including any defects found, were presented to them.

If the customer cannot or will not sign

Tap Customer cannot sign on the customer signature screen and choose Customer unavailable or Customer refused to sign, with an optional note. The check is then finalised with your signature and the recorded reason.

4.7 Completion and the certificate#

After signing, the check is finalised and the certificate is produced:

  • On success you see Inspection completed, the result banner, and a View certificate button. Tap Done to return to the app.
  • If the PDF could not be created, you see Certificate pending with a Retry certificate button. The check itself is finalised — only the PDF needs another attempt. The app also retries whenever the Dashboard opens.
  • When the check recorded work or travel, the screen also offers Delivery note: review and sign (chapter 11).

The app sends nothing to the customer by itself: you share or print the certificate from Reports (§5.3).

5. Reports & certificates#

5.1 The reports list#

Reports lists every completed, signed-off check, newest first (pull to refresh). Each row shows the machine, the customer, date and certificate number, the inspection kind, a Pass / Minor / Fail chip, and the distribution status (Not yet distributed, or Handed off with the date). A voided or superseded certificate is struck through and marked VOID / SUPERSEDED.

Use the search box to find a certificate by customer, machine or certificate number, and the filter chips to narrow the list by result, status, inspection kind or date range; Clear filters resets them. The list shows the newest certificates first; Load more at the bottom brings in older ones (search and filters cover the certificates loaded so far).

5.2 Viewing a certificate#

Tap a report to open the PDF certificate. You can pinch to zoom, swipe through pages, and use the Print and Share controls. A red banner appears across the top if the certificate has been VOIDed or SUPERSEDED. If the signed original has not reached this device yet, the app shows a preview and says so in a banner — sync and reopen to get the original.

The certificate's header, logo, banner image and accent colour come from the company profile it was issued under (§13.3), and the declaration wording from Certificate settings (§13.4). A certificate keeps the look it was issued with; later changes affect only new certificates.

5.3 Distributing a certificate#

From the certificate view, use Share or Print to send the certificate — for example by attaching the PDF to an e-mail from your own mailbox. Record distribution then notes that you have handed the report off. A handoff can be recorded once the certificate has synced; until then the app says it is still syncing.

Good to know

The app records that you handed a report off. It cannot confirm that the customer received it, and it sends no e-mail itself. Each row in Reports shows Not yet distributed until a handoff is recorded.

5.4 Voiding a certificate (Admin, or the Certificates permission)#

Use Void when a certificate was issued in error. The original is kept and clearly marked VOID, and the machine's due date is recalculated from its remaining valid certificates. Voiding cannot be undone.

  1. Open the certificate and tap the Void certificate icon in the title bar.
  2. Enter a reason (required), e.g. “issued in error”.
  3. Re-enter your own password when prompted.

5.5 Superseding / reissuing (Admin, or the Certificates permission)#

Use Supersede when a corrected certificate replaces an earlier one. Both are kept and linked, and the old one is marked SUPERSEDED.

  1. Produce the replacement check and certificate for the same machine.
  2. Open the original certificate, tap the Mark superseded icon in the title bar and enter a reason.
  3. Pick the replacement from the list of that machine's other certificates (identified by date and result) and confirm with Supersede.
  4. Re-enter your own password when prompted.

A superseded certificate can still be voided; a voided one cannot be superseded. Without the permission, the app says that only an administrator, or a user granted the certificates permission, can do this.

Signed certificates are never edited

The only corrections are a void or a supersede. In both cases the original is kept and the action is recorded in the audit log.

6. Bookings & scheduling#

The office plans work through a calendar of bookings. A booking is one customer visit: it links a customer, one or more machines, an assigned inspector, a start and end time, and a status. Each machine on the booking produces its own check and certificate.

6.1 The calendar#

Move between months with the arrows; days with bookings carry a dot and today is outlined. Tap a day to see its bookings below the calendar. Each booking card shows the customer, the start time, how many machines are on the visit, the assigned inspector and a status chip. Tap the card to open the booking: its time, notes and the list of machines. Cancelled bookings are not shown on the calendar.

6.2 Starting work from a booking#

Next to each machine on a booking is a Start button — or Resume if a draft check already exists, or a green tick if that machine's check is already finalised. Tapping it takes you straight into the checklist for that machine. A booking is completed when every machine on it is finalised.

Start from the booking

Start planned work from the booking. A check started from New check on the Dashboard or from the machine's own screen is not linked to the booking and does not count towards completing it.

6.3 Creating or editing a booking (Admin, or the Bookings permission)#

Administrators, and inspectors granted the Bookings permission, tap Edit booking in an open booking, or create one with the “+” button on Bookings, New booking on the Dashboard or Book in Reminders. Everyone else sees the calendar read-only. The booking form:

  1. Choose the Customer (required) — this filters the machine list.
  2. Tick the Machines for the visit (at least one).
  3. Optionally assign an Inspector (or leave Unassigned).
  4. Set the Date, Start time and End time.
  5. When editing an existing booking, set the Status if needed: Planned, In progress, Completed, Cancelled or Rescheduled. Starting a check from the booking moves it to In progress automatically, and finalising the last machine's check moves it to Completed.
  6. Add Notes for site access, contacts, etc., then tap Save booking.

7. Reminders — due & overdue#

Reminders lists machines that need a booking so nothing is forgotten. A machine that already has an open booking is left off the list — it is already scheduled. It has two sections:

  • Overdue — machines past their next-due date with no booking (red), sorted by how overdue they are.
  • Due within 30 days — machines coming due soon with no booking (amber).

Each machine shows its name, customer and a coloured due chip. If you may manage bookings, tap Book on a machine to open the booking form pre-filled with that customer and machine. Pull down to refresh.

A machine's next-due date is the date of its last completed check plus its re-check interval (set on the machine type, adjustable per machine). A Blocking failure brings the next-due date forward. A machine that has never been inspected has no due date and does not appear here — find it in Machines.

8. Customers#

Customers is the register of the organisations you inspect for. Search by name, and toggle Show archived to include archived records. Tap a customer to see their details, their documents and the machines registered to them.

8.1 Creating or editing a customer (Admin, or the Customers & machines permission)#

Add a customer with the “+” button, or edit one from its detail screen. A customer record carries the company name, a contact name and phone, a report e-mail, the address, notes and a preferred certificate language (Deutsch or English). New checks for the customer start in that language, and it can still be changed per check until it is signed (§4.5).

A customer that has machines, bookings, inspections or documents cannot be deleted, only archived, so earlier certificates stay complete. Archiving a customer also archives its machines, and Restore brings both back. A customer with no such records can be removed with the three-dot menu → Delete permanently.

E-mail addresses are for your reference

The Report e-mail and the Billing e-mail are kept on the customer record for your reference. The app does not send e-mail: when you share a PDF, you enter the address in your own mail app.

8.2 Billing details and the customer's documents#

The customer form also carries what a quote or invoice needs: whether the customer is a business (Firma) or a private person (Privat), a customer number, a structured address (street, postcode, city, country), the UID number, a separate billing e-mail, a default payment term, a default reference line, the document language, a contact line for documents and internal billing notes. Payment term and document language can be left on company default.

If the same customer number was given to two different customers on two devices, the list shows a red notice naming the numbers; renumber one of them.

UID numbers are format-checked, not verified

The UID number is checked for its format only. The app cannot tell you whether a UID is valid or belongs to this customer — verify it yourself where the VAT treatment depends on it.

Below the customer's details, a Documents (Belege) section lists their quotes, delivery notes and invoices with number, date and status, and offers New quote / New delivery note / New invoice (quotes and invoices need the Billing permission).

9. Machines & machine types#

9.1 The machine register#

Machines lists every machine. Search by name, serial number or customer, filter with the Overdue and Due soon chips, or sort by due date. Each row shows the machine type icon, the name, the customer, the serial number and a due-date chip. Tap a machine to see its details, a Start inspection button and the machine's History — every check on it. Tap a finished check in the history to open its certificate, or a draft to continue it.

9.2 Creating or editing a machine (Admin, or the Customers & machines permission)#

  1. Tap “+” on Machines (or Edit on a machine's detail).
  2. Choose the Customer and the Machine type (both required; the New type tile creates a type without leaving the form).
  3. Fill in the Label / fleet name, Make, Model, Serial number and Year as available.
  4. Set the Inspection interval override (months) only if this machine differs from its type's default.
  5. Switch on Auto-book next check if the next visit should be booked automatically (see below).
  6. Leave Checklist template on Default for type unless this machine needs its own checklist.
  7. Tap Save.

Auto-book next check

When this switch is on, finalising a check creates the next visit automatically: a Planned booking without an inspector on the machine's new next-due date, which the office then adjusts. A future visit you have already planned for the machine is never doubled.

9.3 Machine types (Admin, or the Customers & machines permission)#

The icon button next to the Machines search box opens Machine types (e.g. Crane, Forklift, Tractor). Each type carries a default checklist template, a default re-check interval, and whether it tracks operating hours and/or kilometres. Tap a type to edit it; its checklist is edited under Templates (chapter 10).

The list warns on a type that has no default checklist or whose checklist is empty: checks for machines of that type cannot start until that is put right under Templates.

10. Checklist templates (Admin)#

Templates (administrators, and inspectors granted the Templates permission) is where the checklists themselves are built. A template belongs to a machine type. A type can have several templates: one is the type's default, and any other can be assigned to individual machines (§9.2).

10.1 Creating and editing a template#

To create a template, tap “+” on Templates, give it a name, choose its machine type and tap Create.

Open a template to edit its items. Each item has a check description, optional guidance / acceptance criteria, and a photo-required switch. Add an item with + Item and edit one by tapping it. The bin icon deletes an item after a confirmation. To reorder, drag an item by the handle at its right edge, then tap Save order. The pencil icon in the title bar renames the template, and the star icon makes it the default checklist for its machine type.

An optional item interval in months can be noted on an item for your reference; it does not change which items a check contains.

Each item can carry its text in both languages. Text in your organisation's working language (set in Certificate settings, §13.4) is required; the other language is optional.

If you leave the other language blank

The editor lists the items that have no text in the other language. The template still works; it only means a certificate in that language cannot be finalised until the text is added (§4.5).

10.2 Editing a template that is in use#

Each check takes its own copy of the template's items when it is started. Editing a template therefore affects only checks started afterwards; earlier and in-progress checks, and their certificates, are unchanged.

10.3 Archiving a template you no longer need#

Open the template, tap the three-dot menu in the title bar and choose Archive template. It disappears from the Templates list and can no longer be chosen for machines or new checks. Past checks and certificates are unaffected.

  • Still in use? Archiving is refused while the template is a machine type's default checklist or is assigned to an active machine. The message names the reason: set another default for the type, or choose another template on those machines, then archive.
  • Changed your mind? Tap Show archived templates at the bottom of the Templates list, open the template and choose Restore template from the three-dot menu.

11. Work & travel → delivery notes#

The work hours, travel time and travel distance an inspector records on the Machine data & time step (§4.4) are added to a delivery note (Lieferschein) automatically when the inspection is finalised — the same figures, on the document the customer signs for.

11.1 What happens at completion#

  • One line per recorded figure — work time, travel time and distance. Each line uses the company profile's default article for work, travel or distance (§13.3), so the invoice built later is already priced. If no default article is set, the line has no price — set it on the invoice. The delivery note itself prints no prices.
  • One note per visit. If a draft delivery note already exists for the same customer, company and day, the new inspection's lines are added to it, so a job with several machines ends with one note. A note that has already been finalised is never changed.
  • The note stays a draft. The completion screen offers Delivery note: review and sign: check the lines and finalise the note (§12.4), then choose the three-dot menu → Sign to take the customer's signature on the device (§12.5). You can also do this later from the Billing tab.
  • Nothing recorded, no note. An inspection without work, travel or distance figures creates no delivery note.
  • Your edits stay. If you remove or replace an inspection's lines in the draft, the app does not put them back.

Tip

Travel is recorded per inspection. On a visit covering several machines, each machine's travel is listed — remove the duplicates in the editor before you finalise the note.

11.2 If the note could not be created#

Creating the note never holds up the inspection. If the note cannot be created (for example because no company profile has been set up yet), the completion screen says so, the Dashboard shows a warning with a Retry now button, and the app tries again each time the Dashboard opens.

If two devices finalise inspections of the same visit before they have synced, each may create its own draft note. Both appear in the Billing tab; discard the one you do not need.

11.3 Work & travel export#

A spreadsheet export of recorded work and travel is on the Billing tab → Delivery notes list: tap Export CSV. It covers the completed inspections in the list's date filter (the current month when no range is set), one row per inspection with its date, customer, machine, inspector, work hours, travel hours, distance and result, and hands the file to your device's share sheet. It is available to every signed-in user.

12. Documents — quotes, delivery notes & invoices#

The Billing tab (Belege in German) is where the office writes quotes (Angebote), delivery notes (Lieferscheine), invoices (Rechnungen) and cancellation invoices (Stornorechnungen). Each document is written in German or English, following the customer's document language.

The tab has three lists: Quotes, Delivery notes and Invoices (cancellation invoices appear under Invoices). Each list has a search box (number, customer or reference), status chips, a date range, a company filter when there is more than one profile, and Load more for older entries.

Every signed-in user sees the Billing tab and can write and sign delivery notes. Quotes, invoices, cancellation invoices and the article catalogue need the Billing permission, which administrators hold and can grant to an inspector (§13.9); without it, quotes and invoices open view-only.

12.1 Before the first invoice: the company profile#

An invoice must name its issuer in full. Open Settings → Company profiles (§13.3) and complete the default profile — name, address, UID number, and bank details if you want them printed. An invoice cannot be finalised while the issuer's name, address or UID is missing (for small-business-exempt invoices, switch on Small business scheme on the profile first). If you move over from another system mid-year, set the number floor per document type so numbering continues where you left off.

12.2 Creating a document#

  • From the Billing tab — open the Quotes, Delivery notes or Invoices list and tap New quote / New delivery note / New invoice, then choose the Customer (and another Issuing company if needed) at the top.
  • From a customer — the New quote / delivery note / invoice buttons on the customer's detail screen (§8.2).
  • From a quote — an open or accepted quote offers Create delivery note and Create invoice; the lines are copied (optional quote lines are left out).
  • From delivery notes — tick several open or signed notes of one customer and company in the list and tap Create invoice from N delivery notes: one combined invoice with a group per note. For a single note, open it and choose the three-dot menu → Create invoice. The notes become Invoiced (Verrechnet) when that invoice is finalised.

The result is always a draft (Entwurf). A draft has no number, can be edited or discarded freely, and can be shared only as a preview marked Entwurf / Draft.

12.3 The editor#

A new document needs a customer before it is saved

Choose the customer first. A new document is saved only once it has a customer; from then on every change is saved automatically. If you leave a new document before choosing a customer, nothing is kept.

Add customer beside the Customer field creates a customer without leaving the editor. The fields depend on the type:

  • Document date, reference / order number, the document language and the VAT treatment (standard; reverse charge; intra-Community supply; small-business exemption; export; or another exemption with your own reason text).
  • Quotes: a valid-until date. Delivery notes: the delivery date (required). Invoices: the service date or period (required) and the delivery note number(s), filled in automatically when the invoice is built from delivery notes.
  • Payment term on quotes and invoices: 8, 14, 21 or 30 days net, On receipt, or No payment term. An invoice's Due on date follows from it and can be adjusted by hand.
  • Opening and closing text, filled in when the document is created from the company profile's texts, and internal notes that are never printed. If you change the document language afterwards, check the opening and closing text — it is not replaced.
  • Lines: Add from article (name, unit, price and VAT rate are copied, then editable) or Add free text. Each line has a description, quantity, unit, net unit price, an optional discount in %, a VAT rate, an optional machine and an optional note; delivery-note lines have no price fields. Quotes can mark a line optional (printed, not totalled). Drag to reorder.
  • The totals (net, VAT per rate, gross) update as you type.

Good to know

The VAT treatment is your decision. Choosing a reverse-charge or exempt treatment sets every line to 0 % VAT and prints the corresponding statutory note on the document; reverse charge and intra-Community supply also require the customer's UID. The app applies these rules — it does not tell you which treatment is correct. Ask your tax adviser if in doubt.

12.4 Finalising a document#

Finalise (Fertigstellen) checks the document and, if everything is in place, gives it its number and locks it. Numbers have the form YYYYNNNN — the year of the document date followed by a running number that restarts each year. Each company profile and each document type has its own sequence.

If something is missing, the app lists it instead of finalising. Every document needs a customer, a document date that is not in the future and at least one line with a description, a quantity and a price that is not negative; a delivery note needs its delivery date. Invoices additionally need the issuer's full details, a usable customer address, the service date or period, and — depending on the amount and the VAT treatment — the customer's UID.

  • A finalised document keeps the issuer and customer details as they were when it was finalised. Later edits to the company profile or the customer do not change it.
  • A finalised document can no longer be edited in the app. Corrections are made by cancellation invoice or void (§12.5).
  • The PDF is created right after finalising. If that fails, the document stays finalised and is marked PDF pending; opening the Billing tab retries it and shows a notice with Retry.
  • On a second device a document may show without the logo or banner until that image has synced to the device; sync first when the header matters.

Invoices are finalised online

The app syncs first before it finalises an invoice or cancellation invoice, so that the number it gives is up to date. Without a connection, finalising an invoice is refused: connect, sync, then try again. Quotes and delivery notes can be finalised offline.

12.5 Statuses and what you can do next#

TypeStatusesActions
QuoteDraft (Entwurf) → Open (Offen) → Accepted (Angenommen) / Rejected (Abgelehnt); Void (Ungültig)Accept or reject; create a delivery note or an invoice from it; void with a reason.
Delivery noteDraft → Open → Signed (Unterschrieben) → Invoiced (Verrechnet); VoidSign on the device (customer signature with name, or record that the customer could not sign and why); combine into an invoice; void while open and unsigned.
InvoiceDraft → Open → Paid (Bezahlt); Cancelled (Storniert); VoidMark paid (date, method, note); cancel with a cancellation invoice; void only while it has not been shared.
Cancellation invoiceDraft → OpenFinal — it cannot be cancelled or voided itself.

The actions are in the three-dot menu of an open document. Mark sent (your own note that you sent it) is available on every finalised document that is not void, for users with the Billing permission.

  • Signing a delivery note (or accepting a quote by signature) adds the recipient's dated signature to the PDF. Signed and invoiced notes can no longer be voided. If you record that the customer could not sign, the reason is stored, the note stays Open and no signature can be added afterwards.
  • Mark paid records the payment date, method (bank transfer, cash, card, other) and a note. Paying by cash shows a reminder that this app is not a cash register: where the law requires a cash-register receipt, issue it from a registered cash register.
  • Cancellation invoice (Stornorechnung): the correct way to undo an invoice that has been sent or paid. Cancel invoice asks for a reason and your password and opens the cancellation invoice as a draft; the original becomes Cancelled / Storniert when you finalise that draft. Issue a corrected invoice afterwards as a new document.
  • Void (Ungültig) is for a document that was never sent. It needs the Billing permission, a reason and your password, and the PDF is marked VOID. The record and its number are kept; the number is not reused. The app refuses to void an invoice that was shared or printed from the app. For quotes and delivery notes it does not check, so void them only if they have not been sent.
  • Discard removes a draft (and only a draft) after confirmation.

12.6 Preview, share and print#

Every document opens a PDF preview. Share / print hands the PDF to another app — e-mail, messenger, printer — and the document records that it was shared. For an invoice or cancellation invoice the button stays disabled until the document has synced once; a Sync now button appears beside it while it waits. The button is also disabled for a voided document, while the PDF is still pending, and while a duplicate number affects the document (§12.7).

The printed invoice carries the issuer and recipient, number, date, service period, quantities and descriptions, net amounts and VAT per rate, the gross total, the UID numbers and — where one applies — the statutory note for the VAT treatment, plus the payment term and due date. Bank details print in the page footer when the profile's footer lines are empty (§13.3); with an IBAN on the profile, a finalised invoice with a positive total also carries a QR code that banking apps scan to pre-fill the transfer.

12.7 Duplicate document numbers#

If two devices each finalise a document while they are not in sync with each other, both can receive the same number. The app notices this at the next sync: a red banner appears on the Dashboard and in the Billing lists, both documents are marked, and neither can be shared or printed until it is resolved. The app never renumbers a document by itself. To resolve it, decide which document stands, void the other and issue it again; the new one receives the next free number.

If the document to withdraw has already been sent, it can only be cancelled with a cancellation invoice, and the notice then remains on both documents — keep the paperwork of both and speak to your administrator.

Tip

Because invoices are finalised online (§12.4), duplicate invoice numbers are rare. Syncing before you finalise a quote or delivery note helps in the same way.

12.8 What the documents feature does not do#

  • It does not verify UID numbers and does not decide the VAT treatment for you.
  • It is not a cash register in the sense of the Austrian RKSV.
  • It produces PDF documents only — no structured e-invoice and no accounting export.
  • Keeping your invoices for the period the law requires, and handing them to your accountant, remain your organisation's tasks.

13. Settings#

Settings is grouped under headings — Account, Appearance & language, Sync & Drive, Security, Administration, Help & about and Danger zone. What you see depends on your role. For a user without administrator permissions, the Administration tiles are folded into one collapsed entry, and locked tiles explain why when tapped. Help & about shows the app version and holds the Privacy policy, the User manual and Show the introduction again (§2.9).

13.1 Profile and language#

The top card shows your name, e-mail and role. Below it, the Language toggle switches the app between English and German, taking effect immediately. It applies to this device — to everyone who signs in on it.

Interface language vs certificate language

The Language toggle changes only what you see on screen. The language a certificate is printed in follows the customer (§8.1) and can be adjusted per check on the summary screen until it is signed (§4.5).

13.2 Appearance — light & dark mode#

The Appearance control sets how the app looks on this device: System (follow the device's own setting), Light, or Dark. It has no effect on certificates or documents.

13.3 Company profiles (Admin / Organisation settings)#

Company profiles (Firmenprofile) describe the companies you issue certificates and documents under. There is always one default profile; add further profiles when you invoice from more than one company. Everyone can view the profiles; editing them needs the Organisation settings permission, which administrators hold. The list has an Add company profile button and a three-dot menu per profile with Set as default and Archive. A profile holds:

  • Display name, legal name, address, phone, e-mail and UID number — the issuer details printed on every document.
  • Bank name, IBAN and BIC — printed in the page footer of documents when you leave the footer lines empty (if you write your own footer lines, include the bank details there). With an IBAN, a finalised invoice with a positive total also carries a QR code for banking apps.
  • Website, company register number, register court and country code — stored for your reference; add them to the footer lines if they must be printed.
  • A logo. Any image from the gallery works; a large image is scaled down automatically. Use a document preview to see the result.
  • Logo size on documents — Small, Medium or Large. The same choice sets the logo size on certificates. The logo is never cropped or stretched.
  • A banner image — letterhead-style artwork printed across the top of every page of quotes, delivery notes, invoices and certificates. Choose its position (left, centred or right) with the buttons that appear once an image is set. On certificates the title row always carries a logo: without your own, the built-in HDX logo is printed — upload a logo if you do not want it.
  • A banner tagline (slogan) — text printed in a coloured strip under the header of quotes, delivery notes and invoices, with its colour and alignment. Leave it empty for no strip.
  • The certificate accent colour — one of eight preset colours.
  • Footer lines — one per line, with an alignment for documents. With no footer lines, documents print a standard footer with your name, address, contact and bank details. On certificates the footer lines replace the standard closing note.
  • Small business scheme — switch it on before issuing small-business-exempt invoices. Whether the scheme applies to you is a question for your tax adviser.
  • Signatory name and title and an optional stored signature, printed on quotes.
  • Default payment term and default document language for new documents.
  • Number floors per document type and year — the first number to issue when you move from another system mid-year. Each is stored with Save floor; a floor below the highest number already issued has no effect.
  • Default articles for work, travel and distance, used for the lines the app adds to a delivery note when an inspection is finalised (chapter 11).
  • Text templates — your own opening and closing wording per document type and language. Left empty, the built-in wording is used.

Documents and certificates already issued keep the details and the look they were issued with. A profile can be archived only while nothing refers to it and it is not the default; an archived profile cannot be restored in the app, so archive only a profile created by mistake. If two devices set different default profiles, a banner asks you to confirm one.

13.4 Certificate settings (Admin)#

Certificate settings (Zertifikatseinstellungen) holds the general settings for PDF certificates; the company identity, logo and colour are on the company profile (§13.3). Here you can set:

  • The default language for new customers (Deutsch or English), which is also the working language for checklist templates (§10.1).
  • How many photos per item appear on the certificate (1–20).
  • Whether to include the photo section and the per-item notes on certificates.
  • Optional inspector and customer declaration wording. If you replace a declaration, supply it in both English and German.

Changes apply to future certificates; certificates already issued keep the settings they were issued with.

13.5 Articles (Admin / Billing)#

Articles (Artikel) is the catalogue of services and materials you put on documents. Each article has an article number (the next free one is suggested), a German name and description (English optional), a unit, a category, the net sale price, an optional purchase price, the VAT rate, and optionally the company profile it belongs to and a linked machine. Search and category chips filter the list. Articles are never deleted: archive one you no longer use; it stays on existing documents and can be restored. If the same article number was given to two articles on two devices, a red notice names the numbers; renumber one.

13.6 Connecting Google and the shared folder (Admin)#

An administrator links Google and points the app at the shared folder (the Drive store):

  1. Under Google account (Drive access), tap Connect and complete the Google sign-in. (This gives the app access to the shared folder only; it is not your app login.)
  2. Under Drive store, either tap Set up Drive store automatically to create or find an “HDX Inspect Data Store” folder in your Drive, or tap the Drive store row to paste a Drive folder ID.

Once Google is connected, the account tile's menu (⋮) offers two more actions:

  • Switch account — connect a different Google account on this device. The configured Drive store is left in place.
  • Disconnect — remove the Google connection from this device. Your Drive files are not deleted; the device simply stops syncing until an account is connected again.

Tip

When you bring an additional device into use, connect the same Google account and the same folder the office already uses. A different account or folder gives the device a separate, empty set of data. The full steps are in §2.3.

Do not use automatic set-up to fix a sync problem

Set up Drive store automatically is for setting up, not for repairing. On a device that already has a Drive store, it asks you to confirm before it switches to a different or new folder — only confirm if you deliberately want a new, separate store. Cancel changes nothing.

If sync is failing, use Re-check Drive store instead: it checks the configured folder and syncs again without changing anything.

If Google reports a problem with the connection, the app shows a message that explains it. Pass that message on to your administrator.

13.7 Sync status and conflicts#

The Synchronisation row shows when the device last synced and whether changes are still waiting; anyone can tap Sync now. If the last sync failed, a Details button shows the error, and a banner under the app header reports it until you dismiss it.

If two devices changed the same record before they had synced with each other, the change waits in Sync conflicts, which any signed-in user can open. Each conflict shows the record and, field by field, the value on This device and the Incoming value. Choose Keep this device or Keep incoming and confirm. The chosen version then applies on every device, and the choice cannot be undone. Changes to different records never conflict.

13.8 Accounts & devices (Admin)#

Accounts & devices is where administrators manage app logins and see the devices in use.

  • Create an account — enter the username, name, optional e-mail, the role (Inspector or Admin — it cannot be changed later) and a temporary password, and pass it to the user yourself; they must replace it at first sign-in.
  • Edit a name, reset a password (by typing a new temporary one), deactivate / reactivate an account, or delete it. Deactivate keeps the account but stops it signing in; Delete removes the login permanently. Either way the person's past inspection records and certificates are kept. The last active administrator cannot be deactivated or deleted, and you delete your own account from the Danger zone (§2.6).
  • Permissions — grant an inspector individual admin abilities (§13.9).
  • Devices — each device appears once someone has signed in on it, with a platform name (for example Android tablet, iPhone, Windows PC), a device code (used in certificate numbers) and when it was last seen. The device you are using is listed first and marked This device. You can mark a device untrusted as a note for your own overview.

A new account or device can take a few minutes to appear on your other devices — each one picks it up at its next sync.

Good to know

Account changes reach a device when it next syncs, so a deactivated account can still sign in on a device that has been offline since the change. Marking a device untrusted does not block it. To stop a lost or retired device from reaching your data, remove its Google account's access to the shared folder in Google Drive.

13.9 Per-user permissions (Admin)#

On an inspector's row, the menu has a Permissions entry that opens a set of switches. Each one grants that inspector one area of the admin tools. Saving requires your admin password.

PermissionWhat it grants
Bookings & planningCreate, edit and cancel bookings.
Customers & machinesCreate and edit customers, machines and machine types.
TemplatesThe Templates tab: create and edit checklist templates.
Certificates: void & supersedeVoid or supersede finalised certificates (password required each time).
BillingQuotes, invoices and cancellation invoices, the article catalogue, the customers' billing details and the Dashboard's billing tiles. Delivery notes need no permission.
Accounts & devicesManage user accounts and devices — including granting these permissions to others.
Organisation settings & device administrationThe Google connection and Drive store, company profiles, certificate settings, data retention and the device wipe.
  • Changes take effect at that user's next sign-in on each device, once the device has synced.
  • Nobody can change their own permissions.
  • At least one active administrator account must always exist; an inspector with every permission does not count as one.

Good to know

An inspector granted Accounts & devices can manage accounts and permissions — treat that grant like making them an administrator.

13.10 Audit log#

Audit log is a read-only list of significant actions — records created or changed, sign-offs, voids, supersedes, exports, distributions and resolved conflicts — newest first, with the time and the account that acted. Any signed-in user can view it. If the screen shows a red warning that entries could not be verified, tell your administrator.

13.11 Danger zone#

The red Danger zone holds the actions that cannot be undone. Delete my account is available to every user (§2.6). The data-retention controls and the device wipe need the Organisation settings permission; for everyone else they are shown locked. All of them ask for your password.

Retention period

Retention period sets how long finalised records are kept before an administrator may delete them. The default is Keep forever. You can choose 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 or 10 years (7 years is marked as the recommended value for Austrian record-keeping). Setting the period deletes nothing by itself, and the setting applies to this device only — set it on the device you will run the clean-up from.

Deleting records past retention

Once a retention period is set, Delete records past retention removes finalised checks older than the period. The app shows how many records will be removed and asks for your password. The deletion then applies on all devices at their next sync, including the checks' photos and PDFs. Customers and machines are not affected.

Wipe this device

Wipe this device deletes the app's database on this device and signs the device out of Google. If there is work that has not synced yet, the app lists what would be lost and stops: cancel and sync first, or choose Force wipe to lose it. Afterwards a final screen offers Close app.

Important — read this

A device wipe affects this device only and cannot be undone. It does not delete anything from your Google Drive, and it does not remove the Google account's access to the shared folder — an administrator does that in Google Drive.

Some files, such as photos and PDFs already saved on the device, can remain after a wipe. Uninstall the app to remove everything from the device.

14. Working offline & sync#

HDX Inspect is built to work without a signal. Everything you do — inspections, bookings, customer and machine changes — is saved on the device straight away. When the device is next online, your changes are sent to your organisation's shared folder and everyone else's changes are fetched.

  • You do not need to do anything. Sync runs by itself while someone is signed in, and you can start it at any time with Sync now in Settings.
  • The sync badge at the top of every main screen shows the state: Online, N queued (changes waiting to be sent), Syncing…, Offline, or a red Sync issue.
  • A dropped connection is not a problem. The app tries again by itself — after a short pause, every few minutes, and as soon as the device is back online. Your work stays on the device until it has been sent.
  • Conflicts are shown to you. If the same record was changed on two devices, a person chooses which version to keep (§13.7).
  • Problems are reported. If the shared folder cannot be reached, the Drive storage is full or the Google connection has expired, the sync badge turns red and Settings shows what to do (chapter 17).

Sync early and often

Sync early and often. Work that exists only on one device is lost if that device is lost, stolen or broken before it has synced. Sync at the end of each visit or working day wherever you can.

Sync runs only while someone is signed in (§2.8).

Good to know

Sync keeps your devices in step; it is not a backup. Arrange a regular backup copy of the shared Google Drive folder to a second location.
